what: Mizuho Financial Group is one of Japan's three megabanks. It takes deposits from Japanese households, lends to Japanese corporations, runs trust and securities businesses, and has built a US investment banking presence.
customers: Japanese households and corporations, institutional investors, and US mid-market corporate clients.
money: Japanese household deposits, loans and asset management
lending and transaction banking for Japanese companies
moat: A core of Japanese corporate relationships going back more than a century, and a deposit base so large it costs almost nothing to fund.
risks: Decades of near-zero Japanese rates kept lending margins very thin
Large holdings of Japanese government bonds lose value as rates rise
Japanese corporate loan demand grows slowly
Overseas expansion competes against entrenched US and European banks
opportunities: The Bank of Japan ending negative rates lifts income on its huge deposit base directly
Revenue grew about 29% last year as rates rose
Selling cross-shareholdings in client companies releases capital for buybacks
watch: Domestic net interest income as Japanese policy rates move, and the pace of cross-shareholding sales.
